Welcome 👋

This interactive guide covers CSE433 Deep Learning, Lectures 1–5 of CMU's 11-785 (Bhiksha Raj): what a neuron computes, why networks need depth, what a network can represent, how it learns (perceptron, ADALINE, empirical risk), the calculus of optimisation, losses, and backpropagation. It also works every problem of Sheet 1 and Assignment 3, and every class poll. Every number in it was computed by code, and where the slides contain a mistake, the guide says so and gives the correct version. Navigate through the modes below:

  • 📖 Tutorial Mode: each step goes idea → worked example → why → quick check, with tap-to-trace tables and eight hands-on labs (gates, K-maps, regions, staircases, the perceptron algorithm, gradient descent, softmax, backprop).
  • 🎴 Flash Cards: definitions, weights, formulas and numbers to know cold.
  • 🎯 Professor's Focus: Part 1 (Lectures 1–2 + Sheet 1) and Part 2 (Lectures 3–5 + Assignment 3), every problem worked in full.
  • ⚡ Practice Quiz: exam-style MCQs for every topic, including every class poll from the slides (the weekly quizzes reuse them).
  • ✍️ Written Practice: exam-style written questions (derive, prove, construct, explain): write your answer, check the numbers, then mark yourself against a model answer. Inside the tutorials, 🧭 guided solves walk you through a full problem one checked line at a time.

💡 Short on time? Do Tutorials 4, 7, 10 and 11: Boolean MLPs, the perceptron algorithm, losses, and backprop hold most of the numbers. Press Ctrl+K to search, and open the 📋 Cheat Sheet (bottom-right) for every formula.

📋 Exam Reference Sheet

History (Lecture 1)

  • Associationism (Aristotle's 4 laws: contiguity, frequency, similarity, contrast) → connectionism: knowledge is in the connections. First proposed by Alexander Bain (1873). Brain ≈ 80 billion neurons, ≈ 100 trillion connections.
  • McCulloch & Pitts (1943): neurons as Boolean logic; inhibitory synapse vetoes firing; no learning rule.
  • Hebb (1949): \(w_{xy} \leftarrow w_{xy} + \eta\, x\, y\). "Fire together, wire together". Unstable: weights only grow (no reduction, no competition). Fix: Sanger's rule \(w_{ij} \leftarrow w_{ij} + \eta\, y_j \bigl(x_i - \sum_{k \le j} w_{ik} y_k\bigr)\).
  • Rosenblatt (1958) perceptron: \(\mathbf w \leftarrow \mathbf w + \eta(d - y)\mathbf x\), provably convergent for linearly separable classes. Minsky & Papert (1969): one unit can't do XOR.
  • Turing (1948): A-type = random NAND nets (no learning); B-type = connections with learnable "modifiers".

The threshold unit

  • \(z = \sum_i w_i x_i + b\), \(y = H(z) = 1\) if \(z \ge 0\) else 0, with \(b = -T\) (\(T\) = threshold). Fires iff \(\sum_i w_i x_i \ge T\).
  • Linear: \(3x + 7y\) (no constant). Affine: linear + constant, \(3x + 7y + 4\). (Every linear function is also affine.)
  • AND: \(\mathbf w = (1, 1),\ T = 2\) · OR: \((1, 1),\ T = 1\) · NOT: \(w = -1,\ T = 0\) · NAND: \((-1, -1),\ T = -1\).
  • Universal AND (\(X_1, \dots, X_L\) plain, \(X_{L+1}, \dots, X_N\) negated): weights \(+1/-1\), \(T = L\). Universal OR: \(T = L - N + 1\). At least K of the desired polarity: \(T = L - N + K\).
  • A single unit is a linear classifier: boundary \(\mathbf w^\top \mathbf x + b = 0\), \(\mathbf w\) points to the side that fires.

XOR and depth

  • No single unit computes XOR (needs \(w_1 \ge T,\ w_2 \ge T,\ T \gt 0,\ w_1 + w_2 \lt T\): contradiction).
  • 3 units: \(h_1\) = OR \((1, 1, T = 1)\), \(h_2\) = NAND \((-1, -1, T = -1)\), out = AND \((1, 1, T = 2)\).
  • 2 units (skip connections): \(h = \text{AND}(x, y)\) (\(T = 2\)); out: \(x + y - 2h \ge 1\).
  • Depth = longest path from a source (input) to a sink (output). "Deep" = depth > 2 (≥ 3 layers). Layer = all neurons at the same depth.

Boolean functions as MLPs (Lecture 2)

  • Any truth table → DNF (one AND term per 1-row) → one hidden layer of AND units + an OR output. So one hidden layer is a universal Boolean function.
  • K-map grouping reduces the DNF → fewer hidden units (L2 p47: 7 terms → 3: \(\bar Y \bar Z + \bar W X \bar Y + \bar X Y \bar Z\)).
  • Worst case (checkerboard = parity, nothing groups): \(2^{N-1}\) hidden units, \(2^{N-1} + 1\) in all. \(N = 10\) → 512.
  • Deep XOR network: \(3(N - 1)\) perceptrons (\(2(N - 1)\) with the 2-unit XOR), arranged in \(2 \log_2 N\) layers (pairing tree).
  • Only K hidden layers: \(O(2^{CN})\) neurons in the K-th layer, \(C = 2^{-(K-1)/2}\).
  • Parity \(\notin \mathrm{AC}^0\): a constant-depth AND/OR circuit for parity needs super-polynomial (in fact exponential, \(2^{\Omega(n^{1/(d-1)})}\)) size; the slide writes \(2^{n^{1/d}}\). Shannon: almost all \(n\)-input functions need \(\gt 2^n/n\) gates whatever the depth.
  • Threshold circuits: parity in depth 2 with \(O(n^2)\) weights, depth \(\log n\) with \(O(n)\). Parameters = number of connections.

Decision regions

  • Convex polygon with \(N\) edges = \(N\) edge units + AND (\(\sum_i y_i \ge N\)). Hexagon: 7 units. Region sums: \(N\) inside, \(N-1\) past one edge, \(N-2\) past two…
  • Non-convex / disjoint regions: AND each convex piece, OR the pieces → 2 hidden layers.
  • One hidden layer is enough in the limit: many-sided polygon ≈ circle with \(\sum = N\) inside, \(N/2\) outside; bias \(-N/2\) → \(N/2\) inside, 0 outside; fill any shape with circles (\(K \to \infty\)). MLPs are universal classifiers.
  • \(\sum_i y_i = N\Bigl(1 - \frac{1}{\pi} \arccos\bigl(\min(1, r/\lVert \mathbf x - \mathbf c \rVert)\bigr)\Bigr)\).
  • Depth helps: 16-line grid → 56 hidden (16 + 40) with 2 layers, 61 as an XOR tree (46 with 2-unit XOR); 64 lines → 608 (64 + 544) vs 253 (190). Second layer \(\lfloor (N+2)^2/8 \rfloor\).

Real-valued functions

  • Pulse: \(H(x - T_1) - H(x - T_2)\) is 1 on \([T_1, T_2)\). Sum scaled pulses → any 1-D function; cylinders → any N-D function. Universal approximator (one hidden layer, linear/summing output).
  • Staircase for \(x^2\) on \([0, 1]\): \(c_j = (2j - 1)/K^2\), error \(\le (2K - 1)/K^2 \lt 2/K\); \(K = 200\) for \(10^{-2}\).
  • Approximation ≠ exact representation. Output activation fixes the range: threshold \(\{0,1\}\), sigmoid \((0,1)\), tanh \((-1,1)\), ReLU \([0,\infty)\), softplus \((0,\infty)\).
  • Every layer must be wide enough: fewer than 16 threshold units can't capture the 16-line pattern; graded activations (ReLU) pass more information so narrow layers + depth can compensate.
  • VC dimension: threshold nets ∝ number of weights; piecewise-linear ∝ (weights)².

Learning (Lecture 3)

  • Learning = choosing \(W\) so \(f(X; W) \approx g(X)\). True risk \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{div}(f(X; W), g(X))]\) needs \(g\) everywhere → use samples: empirical risk \(\operatorname{Loss}(W) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_i \operatorname{div}(f(X_i; W), d_i)\). ERM: \(\hat W = \arg\min_W \operatorname{Loss}(W)\).
  • Perceptron algorithm (±1 labels): if \(\operatorname{sign}(W^\top x_i) \ne y_i\) then \(W \leftarrow W + y_i x_i\). Converges after \(\le (R/\gamma)^2\) mistakes for separable data (\(W_0 = 0\); \(R\) = longest \(x\); \(\gamma\) = margin). Never converges if not separable.
  • Augment: \(\tilde{\mathbf x} = [\mathbf x, 1]\), \(\tilde{\mathbf w} = [\mathbf w, b]\) → boundary through the origin of the bigger space; \(W \perp\) boundary, points to the + class.
  • MLP with threshold units can't be trained by the perceptron rule: hidden targets unknown → exponential relabelling search.
  • ADALINE: \(\delta = d - z\) (before the threshold); \(\mathbf w \leftarrow \mathbf w + \eta\delta\mathbf x\) (delta / LMS rule) = gradient step on \(\tfrac12 (d - z)^2\). Perceptron: \(\delta = d - y\).
  • Generalized delta rule: \(\delta = d - y\), \(\mathbf w \leftarrow \mathbf w + \eta\,\delta\, f'(z)\,\mathbf x\) (Widrow–Hoff).
  • MADALINE: on error, flip the hidden unit whose \(z\) is closest to 0; keep the flip if the error drops and ADALINE-train that unit toward it. Greedy, small nets only.
  • Threshold units: zero derivative almost everywhere → no direction to move. Fix: differentiable activation + differentiable divergence. Sigmoid output = \(P(Y = 1 \mid X)\) (logistic regression).

Derivatives (Lecture 4)

  • \(\Delta y \approx f'(x)\Delta x\). Scalar of vector: \(\Delta y = \nabla_{\mathbf x} y\, \Delta \mathbf x\) with \(\nabla_{\mathbf x} y\) a 1 × N row; the gradient is its transpose (column).
  • Gradient = direction of fastest increase; −gradient = fastest decrease; ⊥ to level curves; 0 at optima.
  • Min of \(f(x)\): \(f' = 0\) and \(f'' \gt 0\) (sufficient). Multivariate: \(\nabla f = 0\) and Hessian \(\mathbf H\) positive definite (all eigenvalues \(\gt 0\)).
  • Example: \(f = x_1^2 + x_1(1 - x_2) + x_2^2 - x_2 x_3 + x_3^2 + x_3\) → minimum at \((-1, -1, -1)\), Hessian eigenvalues \(2 - \sqrt2,\ 2,\ 2 + \sqrt2\).

Gradient descent

  • \(\mathbf x_{k+1} = \mathbf x_k - \eta_k \nabla f(\mathbf x_k)^\top\) (ascent: +). Stop when \(|f(\mathbf x_{k+1}) - f(\mathbf x_k)| \lt \varepsilon_1\) or \(\lVert \nabla f \rVert \lt \varepsilon_2\).
  • Convex (bowl) + suitable \(\eta\) → global min. Non-convex → local min or inflection point.
  • Training: \(W \leftarrow W - \eta \nabla \operatorname{Loss}(W)^\top\), \(\operatorname{Loss} = \frac{1}{T} \sum_t \operatorname{Div}(Y_t, d_t)\).

Activations and derivatives

  • \(\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})\), \(\sigma' = \sigma(1 - \sigma)\) · \(\tanh' = 1 - \tanh^2\) · \(\operatorname{ReLU}'(z) = 1\) (\(z \ge 0\)), 0 (\(z \lt 0\)) · softplus \(\log(1 + e^{z})\), derivative \(\sigma(z)\).
  • Softmax \(y_i = e^{z_i} / \sum_j e^{z_j}\) (a vector activation): \(\partial y_j / \partial z_i = y_i(\delta_{ij} - y_j)\).

Outputs and divergences

  • Real outputs: L2 \(\operatorname{Div} = \tfrac12 \lVert Y - d \rVert^2\), \(\partial / \partial y_i = y_i - d_i\).
  • Binary (sigmoid): \(\operatorname{Div} = -d \log Y - (1 - d) \log(1 - Y)\); \(\partial / \partial Y = -1/Y\) (\(d = 1\)), \(1/(1 - Y)\) (\(d = 0\)). Not 0 at the minimum.
  • Multi-class (softmax, one-hot \(d\)): \(\operatorname{KL} = \sum_i d_i \log(d_i/y_i) = -\log y_c\); \(\partial / \partial y_c = -1/y_c\), 0 elsewhere.
  • \(\operatorname{Xent} = -\sum_i d_i \log y_i = \operatorname{KL} + H(d)\) (slide p95 writes \(-H(d)\): sign slip); equal for one-hot.
  • Label smoothing: target \(1 - (K - 1)\varepsilon\) at the class, \(\varepsilon\) elsewhere.
  • Softmax + KL, or linear + L2: \(\nabla_{\mathbf z} \operatorname{Div} = (\mathbf y - \mathbf d)^\top\).

Scalar backprop (Lecture 5)

  • Chain rule: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \sum_i \frac{\partial y}{\partial z_i} \frac{dz_i}{dx}\), summed over every path (influence diagram).
  • Forward: \(z_j^{(k)} = \sum_i w_{ij}^{(k)} y_i^{(k-1)}\) (\(y_0 = 1\) for the bias), \(y_j^{(k)} = f_k(z_j^{(k)})\). Store everything.
  • Output: \(\partial \operatorname{Div} / \partial y_i^{(N)} = \partial \operatorname{Div}(Y, d) / \partial y_i\); \(\partial \operatorname{Div} / \partial z_i = f'(z_i)\, \partial \operatorname{Div} / \partial y_i\).
  • Weights: \(\frac{\partial \operatorname{Div}}{\partial w_{ij}^{(k)}} = y_i^{(k-1)} \frac{\partial \operatorname{Div}}{\partial z_j^{(k)}}\) (bias: input 1).
  • Down one layer: \(\frac{\partial \operatorname{Div}}{\partial y_i^{(k-1)}} = \sum_j w_{ij}^{(k)} \frac{\partial \operatorname{Div}}{\partial z_j^{(k)}}\).
  • Vector activation: \(\frac{\partial \operatorname{Div}}{\partial z_i} = \sum_j \frac{\partial \operatorname{Div}}{\partial y_j} \frac{\partial y_j}{\partial z_i}\). Max: 1 for the argmax, 0 else. ReLU at 0: any subgradient in \([0, 1]\).
  • Backprop computes the derivatives; gradient descent uses them to train.

Vector form

  • \(\mathbf z_k = W_k \mathbf y_{k-1} + \mathbf b_k\), \(\mathbf y_k = f_k(\mathbf z_k)\); \(W_k\) is \(D_k \times D_{k-1}\).
  • Jacobian \(J_{\mathbf y}(\mathbf z) = [\partial y_i / \partial z_j]\) (diagonal for scalar activations). Chain rule: outer derivative first, \(\nabla_{\mathbf x} \mathbf y = \nabla_{\mathbf z} \mathbf y\, \nabla_{\mathbf x} \mathbf z\).
  • For \(\mathbf z = W\mathbf y + \mathbf b\): \(\nabla_{\mathbf y} D = \nabla_{\mathbf z} D \cdot W\), \(\nabla_W D = \mathbf y\, \nabla_{\mathbf z} D\), \(\nabla_{\mathbf b} D = \nabla_{\mathbf z} D\) (shapes are transposes of \(W\) and \(\mathbf b\)).
  • Backward loop \(k = N, \dots, 1\): \(\nabla_{\mathbf z_k} = \nabla_{\mathbf y_k} J_{\mathbf y_k}(\mathbf z_k)\); \(\nabla_{\mathbf y_{k-1}} = \nabla_{\mathbf z_k} W_k\); \(\nabla_{W_k} = \mathbf y_{k-1} \nabla_{\mathbf z_k}\); \(\nabla_{\mathbf b_k} = \nabla_{\mathbf z_k}\).
  • Update: \(W_k \leftarrow W_k - \frac{\eta}{T} (\nabla_{W_k} \operatorname{Loss})^\top\), \(\mathbf b_k \leftarrow \mathbf b_k - \frac{\eta}{T} (\nabla_{\mathbf b_k} \operatorname{Loss})^\top\) (p195 wrongly reuses \(\nabla W\)).

Final answers (each one is worked in the tutorials and Professor's Focus)

  • Sheet 1 P1: w = (1, −1, 1, −1, 1, −1), b = −1 (threshold 1 = L − N + K = 3 − 6 + 4)
  • Sheet 1 P2: no single unit (w₁ ≥ T, w₂ ≥ T, T > 0 vs w₁ + w₂ < T); 2 hidden: OR (1, 1, b = −1) and NAND (−1, −1, b = 1), output AND (1, 1, b = −2)
  • Sheet 1 P3: DNF: 2^(N−1) = 128 hidden units for N = 8; tree: 7 XOR modules, 14 hidden units inside them, 3 stages; O(N) modules
  • Sheet 1 P4: F = x̄₂x̄₄ + x₂x₄ (XNOR of x₂, x₄): 8 hidden units → 2
  • Sheet 1 P5: 4 rectangles [−2,2]×[−2,−1], [−2,2]×[0,1], [−2,−1]×[−1,0], [1,2]×[−1,0]; 16 half-space units + 4 AND + 1 OR
  • Sheet 1 P6: c₀ = 0, cⱼ = (2j − 1)/K²; error ≤ (2K − 1)/K² < 2/K; K = 200; approximation only, not exact
  • Sheet 1 P7: (a) T (b) F (c) F (d) T (e) F (f) F
  • Assignment 3 P1: one update (sample 1, pass 1) → w̃ = [2, 1, 1]; boundary 2x₁ + x₂ + 1 = 0; R = √6 ≈ 2.4495
  • Assignment 3 P2: z = 0.8, y = 1, δ_P = 0, δ_A = 0.2; perceptron unchanged, ADALINE → [0.34, −0.42, −0.18]
  • Assignment 3 P3: unit 2 (|z| = 0.15); output 1 → 0; w₂ ← w₂ + η(d₂ − w₂ᵀx)x
  • Assignment 3 P4: w* = Σxd / Σx² = 30.2 / 30 ≈ 1.0067
  • L4 p35–37 example: minimum at (−1, −1, −1), f = −1, Hessian eigenvalues 0.586, 2, 3.414
